• **Word**: Collection of 2 Bytes.

questions.question: ‘Daskathia’ is a form of ballad singing prevalent in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Daskathia is a form of ballad singing prevalent in Odisha.**
 
• Daskathia is a name derived from a unique musical instrument called “Kathi” or “Ram Tali”, wooden clappers used during the presentation.
 
• The performance is a form of worship and offering on behalf of the “Das”, the devotee.
 
• This folk form is mainly associated with the worship of Lord Shiva and thus, during the performances, dedications to Lord Shiva, mentioning its various forms like Rudra, Hara, Mahadeva, Shankar, and Bholanath etc., is prescribed.
 
• The performance group consists of two people, a chief singer (**Gayaka**) and the other known as the '**Palia**'. 
 
• **The Palia plays a second fiddle to the singer, in acting and singing. **

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The President submits his resignation to the Vice-President.
The President submits his resignation to the Prime Minister.
The President submits his resignation to the Chief Justice of India.
The President submits his resignation to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 56** of the Indian Constitution makes it clear that the term of the President is five years from the date on which he enters the office.
 
• His term may be terminated earlier 
 
 
• By a resignation addressed to the Vice-President, or 
 
• By removal by impeachment for violation of the constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 61:** Procedure for impeachment of the President.
 
 
• When a President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by either House of the Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following environmental movements/conflicts of India was directly related to the prevention of felling of trees?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Chipko Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chipko movement was the uprising against the felling of trees and sustaining the ecological balance started in Uttar Pradesh’s Chamoli district (now Uttarakhand) in 1973.**
 
• The name of the movement ‘chipko’ comes from the word ’embrace’. Hugged the trees and encircled them to prevent being hacked.
 
• Sundarlal Bahuguna, a famous Gandhian, is said to have started this movement to guard the trees on the Himalayan slopes. Bahuguna is also known for coining the Chipko slogan **‘ecology is the permanent economy’.**
 
• The movement’s biggest victory was making people aware of their rights to forests, and how grassroots activism can influence policy-making regarding ecology and shared natural resources.
 
• It was a silent, non-violent protest condemning ecological destruction.

questions.question: The ______ layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles). This part of the atmosphere is the densest and almost all weather is in this region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The air is one of the essential conditions for the existence of life on this planet. The air is a mixture of various gases and it encompasses the earth from all sides. The air surrounding the earth is called the atmosphere.**
 
• **Troposphere**:
 
 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• The layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles).
 
• The troposphere contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• This is the most important layer of the atmosphere because all kinds of weather changes take place only in this layer.
 
• The zone dividing troposphere from the stratosphere is known as the tropopause.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Stratosphere:

 
 
• ​It lies beyond troposphere, up to an altitude of 50 km from the earth’s surface.
 
• The temperature in this layer remains constant for some distance but then rises to reach a level of 0°C at 50 km altitude.
 
• This rise is due to the presence of ozone.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomenon, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes. ​
 
 
 
• Mesosphere: 
 
 
• ​This is an intermediate layer beyond the ozone layer and continues up to an altitude of 80 km from the earth’s surface.
 
• The temperature gradually falls to -100°C at 80 km altitude.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from the space.
 
 
 
• Thermosphere:
 
 
• ​In the thermosphere, the temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The ionosphere is a part of this layer.
 
• It extends between 80-400 km. This layer helps in radio transmission.
 
 
 
• Exosphere:​
 
 
• This is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere extending beyond the ionosphere above a height of about 400 km.
 
• The air is extremely rarefied and the temperature gradually increases through the layer.
 
• Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.

questions.question: Which of the following carries blood from the heart to the kidneys?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Renal artery**__.

__
 
• **Renal Arteries carry unfiltered blood from the aorta to the kidneys**__.
 
• The arteries are obscured by the renal veins; they are dorsal to the renal veins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **blood travels** to each kidney through the Renal artery.

 
 
• Renal arteries usually originate from the left inside of the abdominal aorta, directly below the upper mesenteric artery, and supply blood to the kidneys.
 
• It holds half of the overall blood supply to the kidneys.
 
• Up to a third of the overall cardiac production will pass through the kidney-filtering renal arteries.
 
• A capillary is a small blood vessel with a diameter of between 5 and 10 micrometres (μm).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **renal artery** is the branch of the abdominal aorta that carries blood to the kidney.

 
 
• It enters in the kidney through the hilum part.
 
 
 
• The **pulmonary artery** is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood. It carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
 
• The **hepatic artery** is a blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the liver, duodenum, pancreas, and gallbladder.
 
• **Carotid arteries** are major blood vessels in the neck that supply blood to the brain, neck, and face.

questions.question: Hardwood trees like sal, teak, neem and shisham (useful for making furniture, transport and constructional material) are found in which type of forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Deciduous Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests**:

 
 
• They are also called the monsoon forests, these are the most widespread forests in India.
 
• The term ‘Deciduous’ relates to the ability of some plants to lose their leaves annually.
 
• They are spread over regions which receive rainfall between 70 and 200 cm.
 
• **Important Species: **The common trees are Sal, Teak, Sandalwood, neem, Ajun, Ebony, Shisham, Hurra, Mahua, Amla, Semul, Mulberry and Kusum.
 
• It is found on the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats, eastern coastal plains, eastern plateaus, Himalayan foothills and in some parts of the Satluj-Ganga plains, Eastern Rajasthan, Kathiawar, rain-shadow areas of the Deccan plateau, central India and Punjab.

questions.question: Who among the following formulates the monetary policy in India?

options.text: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has released the Monetary Policy Report.
 
• The Monetary Policy Report is issued by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of RBI.
 
• The main aim of monetary policy is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth as price stability is a fundamental precondition for sustainable economic growth. 
 
• In India, the RBI plays an essential role in controlling inflation through the consultation process regarding inflation targeting. The current inflation-targeting framework in India is flexible.
 
• The MPC is a statutory and institutionalized framework under the RBI Act, 1934, for sustaining price stability, while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• The MPC decides the policy interest rate (repo rate) required to achieve the inflation target (4%).
 
• The Governor of RBI is the ex-officio Chairman of the MPC.
 
• It includes CRR, SLR, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, etc.

questions.question: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was enacted by Parliament vide ______Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 on 8th September 2016.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**101st**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insertion of new article 246A**:

 
 
• Notwithstanding anything contained in articles 246 and 254, Parliament, and, subject to clause (2), the Legislature of every State, have power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax imposed by the Union or by such State.
 
• Parliament has exclusive power to make laws with respect to Goods and Service Tax (GST) where the supply of Goods and Services or both takes place in the course of interstate trade or commerce.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **About GST**:

 
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a value-added tax levied on most goods and services sold for domestic consumption.
 
• The GST is paid by consumers, but it is remitted to the government by the businesses selling the goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Legislation on GST**:
 
 
• In India, GST Bill was first introduced in 2014 as The Constitution (122nd Amendment) Bill.
 
• This got an approval in 2016 and was renumbered in the statute by Rajya Sabha as The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016.
 
 
• Central GST to cover Excise duty, Service tax etc, State GST to cover VAT, luxury tax etc.
 
• Integrated GST to cover inter-state trade. IGST per se is not a tax but a system to coordinate state and union taxes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of memory and is similar to RAM?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cache**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Cache memory** is an extremely fast memory type that serves as a buffer between RAM and the CPU.
 
• It holds usually requested data and instructions so that they are immediately available to the CPU when needed.
 
• Cache memory is used to reduce the average time to access data from the Main memory.
 
• **RAM**, which stands for random-access memory, which temporarily stores data while the central processing unit (CPU) is doing other tasks. 
 
• With more RAM on the computer, the less the CPU has to read data from the external or secondary memory (storage device), allowing the computer to run faster. 
 
• RAM is fast though it is volatile, which means it will not retain data if there is no power. It is therefore important to save data to the storage device before the system is turned off.
 
• RAM and Cache memories are both volatile.

questions.question: Robert has sandy soil in his fields. The ideal crop for his field is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Corn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sandy Soil** is light, warm, dry and tends to be acidic and low in nutrients. 
 
• Sandy soils are often known as light soils due to their high proportion of sand and little clay.
 
• These soils have fast water drainage and are easy to work with.
 
• It mainly consists of rock particles such as limestone, shale, granite and quartz.
 
• Sandy Soil has a low percentage of organic material. Water travels through sandy soil very easily, so nutrients leach out quickly.
 
• Vegetable plants that thrive in sandy soil are Carrots, Radishes, Potatoes, Lettuce, Collard greens, Tomatoes, Zucchini, **Corn**, Asparagus, Watermelon, Beans, and Cucumber.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Joaquin Phoenix won the** ‘Golden Globe 2020’ award for ‘Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama’.**
 
• **Golden Globe Award**, any of the awards presented annually by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association (HFPA) in recognition of outstanding achievement in motion pictures and television during the previous year.
 
• Within the entertainment industry, the Golden Globes are considered second in importance both to the Academy Awards for the films and to the Emmy Awards for television, and the televised awards ceremony is a comparably lavish affair.
 
• The presentation of the awards began **in 1944 as an attempt of the newly formed Hollywood Foreign Correspondents Association, a consortium of entertainment journalists based in Los Angeles but working for publications outside the United States.**
